scope: Local iOS steel-pipe-end counting mode; no App Store upload/submission/pricing changes.
features: Default skewer category delegates to the unchanged StickDetector; steel_pipes routes exclusively to PipeDetector.
History records persist category; legacy records missing category decode as skewers; unknown category values fail decoding rather than relabel old history.
Category switching invalidates generation, cancels active reservations, rejects late reservation responses, and prevents late inference results from debiting or replacing the new mode.
Existing unsaved-result confirmation covers category changes; restoring history selects its saved category; reset keeps the current category.
Bilingual category selector, pipe-end photography/review guidance, automatic reference region, manual editing, history labels and category-aware export caption.
The pipe detector never invokes the skewer model, OCR isolation heuristic, Hough circles, or an external photo API.
Pipe automatic reference area is the union of all valid detections; separate bundles and isolated pipes are retained.
Missing/incompatible model/settings/unsupported output fail without consuming a count. A successful zero result retains the existing one-use debit rule.
CountingAccess.swift and original detector/region/model files are byte-identical to HEAD.

modelContract.confidenceThreshold: Pending frozen validation selection; no guessed config shipped
modelContract.preprocessing: PhotoProcessing upright <=2048 image, explicit 1024 square gray114 centered letterbox, nearest-even resized geometry and round(halfPadding-0.1), then Vision scaleFill on the already square image. Inverse removes padding and gain.
modelContract.coreML: Vision VNRecognizedObjectObservation; model NMS; optional Double confidenceThreshold/iouThreshold; no assumption that padded confidence channel dimension equals 1.
limits: No actual pipe CoreML artifact has been delivered yet, so this build fails closed for automatic pipe counts.
CoreGraphics high-quality resize is not asserted pixel-identical to OpenCV; actual App preprocessing/ML prediction parity remains an integration requirement.
No steel-pipe accuracy, real-device latency, or physical-camera validation claimed.
